en: National hero Jose Rizal spoke 22 languages and secretly sent specimens of rare animals to scientists in Europe while exiled in Dapitan.
Filipino women won the right to vote in a 1937 plebiscite, making the Philippines a pioneer in Asian women's suffrage.
Although the sampaguita is the national flower, the rare waling-waling orchid is officially recognized as the Queen of Philippine Orchids.
The 2,000-year-old Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people using only hand tools and ancient irrigation systems.
Before the Spanish arrived, Filipinos wrote on bamboo and leaves using Baybayin, an ancient alphabet where each symbol represents a syllable.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator and was the first woman admitted to Harvard Medical School.
Aklan’s Ati-Atihan is known as the Mother of All Philippine Festivals because its 13th-century origins inspired later celebrations like Sinulog and Dinagyang.
General Emilio Aguinaldo declared Philippine independence on June 12, 1898, from the window of his house in Kawit, Cavite, while the national anthem played.
The Philippine eagle, our national bird, is one of the largest in the world and uniquely possesses a shaggy crest of dark feathers.
The tradition of bayanihan literally means being a bayan and originally involved an entire community physically carrying a traditional nipa hut to a new location.
The Philippine flag is uniquely designed to be flown with the red stripe on top to indicate a state of war.
National Artist Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition for his massive painting Spoliarium, proving Filipino artistic excellence to the world.
